delete.description:
Detaches the vendor's active DID, writing a VendorDIDHistory row that preserves the original assignedAt. The number returns to the spare pool unless the reason is spam_flagged, in which case it is retired.

**Notes:** No handler-level auth check. DELETE requires a JSON body. After release the vendor falls back to the shared DID.

post.summary: Compute enrichment metrics for a page of vendors
post.description:
Given up to 100 vendorIds and a date window, returns per-vendor pickup rate, up/down trend versus the preceding window, rank within their city, flag/error count with the most common reason, top three device models handled, new-vendor flag and hold schedule.

**Notes:** No auth. Companion to /api/getallvendors. Cached in Redis for 60s keyed by window + sorted vendor id set. A call counts as answered at callDuration >= 5s; new-vendor threshold is 30 days; trend threshold is +/-5%.

_Source: `app/api/vendors/enrichments/route.ts`_

get.summary: Proxy list/read in-app banner admin endpoints
get.description:
Optional catch-all server-side proxy to CashkrBackend's /admin/notifications API. With no segments it lists banners; with segments it targets a single banner or its sub-resources (:id, :id/toggle, :id/stats). Query string is forwarded verbatim and the upstream status and payload are passed through untouched.

**Notes:** Proxies to process.env.BACKEND_API || NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (default http://backend.internal:8083/api/v1) at /admin/notifications. Sends the admin's session accessToken plus the internal service token via adminGatewayHeaders. Any upstream status (incl. 422 validation errors) is relayed as-is.

post.description:
Sends an announcement or urgent alert to every vendor via CashkrBackend's broadcast endpoint (an FCM topic push plus an in-app inbox row), then records an AdminActivityLog BROADCAST entry so ck-admin has its own send history.

**Notes:** IRREVERSIBLE side effect: pushes to every vendor and cannot be recalled. Calls POST {NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/admin/vendor-notifications/broadcast with the session accessToken, x-admin-request and x-internal-service-token. Logging failures never fail the send.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
